Subject:       Response to Request for Additional Information Regarding Emergency License
               Amendment Request: One-Time-Use Amendment to Allow Alternative Fuel
               Handling Method for the Recovery of Fuel Assembly DD41



By letter dated September 30, 2026 (Reference 1), in accordance with Title 10 of the Code of
Federal Regulations (10 CFR) 50.90, Application for amendment of license, construction permit,
or early site permit and 10 CFR 50.91, Notice for public comment; State consultation, Palisades
Energy, LLC (Palisades Energy) requested U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC)
approval of a one-time emergency change to the Renewed Facility Operating License (RFOL)
for Palisades Nuclear Plant (PNP). The proposed License Amendment Request (LAR) would
revise UFSAR Sections 9.11 Fuel Handling and Storage Systems, and 14.19 Fuel Handling
Accident, to facilitate transport of fuel assembly DD41 from the reactor utilizing different plant
equipment and following a different travel path than is described in the Updated Final Safety
Analysis Report (UFSAR).

On October 1, 2026, the NRC and Palisades Energy conducted a conference call in which the
NRC staff verbally and visually requested information in the form of questions related to the
proposed LAR. On October 2, 2026, a follow-up conference call was conducted between the
NRC and Palisades Energy. The purpose of the call was to provide verbal responses to the
questions raised and to identify responses required to be docketed .

The enclosure to this letter provides Palisades Energy's responses to the questions that the
NRC and Palisades Energy mutually agreed require a docketed response.

This letter contains no new regulatory commitments and no revisions to existing regulatory
commitments.

If you have any questions regarding this submittal, please contact Kyle Steffie, Regulatory
Assurance Manager, at (269) 290-8915.

                             Response to Request for Information

Background:

By letter dated September 30, 2026, in accordance with Title 10 of the Code of Federal
Regulations (10 CFR) 50.90, Application for amendment of license, construction permit, or early
site permit and 10 CFR 50.91, Notice for public comment; State consultation, Palisades Energy,
LLC (Palisades Energy) requested U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) approval of a
one-time emergency change to the Renewed Facility Operating License (RFOL) for Palisades
Nuclear Plant (PNP). The proposed License Amendment Request (LAR) would revise UFSAR
Sections 9.11 Fuel Handling and Storage Systems, and 14.19 Fuel Handling Accident, to
facilitate transport of fuel assembly OD41 from the reactor utilizing different plant equipment and
following a different travel path than is described in the Updated Final Safety Analysis Report
(UFSAR).

On October 1, 2026, the NRC and Palisades Energy conducted a conference call in which the
NRC staff verbally and visually requested information in the form of questions related to the
proposed LAR. On October 2, 2026, a follow-up conference call was conducted between the
NRC and Palisades Energy. The purpose of the call was to provide verbal responses to the
questions raised and to identify responses required to be docketed .

The following are the NRC's questions and Palisades Energy's responses to the questions that
the NRC and Palisades Energy mutually agreed require a docketed response.



Questions:

   1. In the License Amendment Request section 3.2.1, Dose Comparisons, it is stated, the
      two conditions that are evaluated are normal conditions as designed, as well as
      conditions from an accidental drop of the canister that assumes a complete loss of
      neutron and gamma shielding . The Dose Evaluation for the Fuel Transfer Canister
      executive summary (Reference 1) states that for a drop accident no damage to the
      canister is expected that would have significant impact on dose rates and that dose rates
      around the canister are expected to be essentially the same as for normal conditions .
      Was an analysis performed for an accidental drop of the canister assuming a complete
      loss of neutron and gamma shielding? If so, are the dose rates around the canister still
      expected to be essentially the same as normal conditions?

   2. Will Palisades Energy be performing a survey (Chemistry Sample) of the fuel assembly
      just before the top of the Fuel Transfer Canister (FTC) is placed to ensure that
      movement of the assembly did not cause loss of integrity of any of the fuel rods?

   3. Please confirm that the load path does not cross fuel assemblies within the reactor and
      that load paths within the Spent Fuel Pool Building are consistent with standard cask
      handling. Also, confirm that the safe load path does not travel in the vicinity of safe
      shutdown Structures, Systems and Components (SSCs).

Page 3 of 4



  4. Please confirm that the bundle integrity has been confirmed/assessed to support the
     planned lift from the reactor vessel to ensure fuel rod bundle integrity and prevent
     damage.



Responses:

   1. Yes. A draft analysis was performed assuming total loss of neutron and gamma
      shielding. However, following the positive results from the FTC Drop Analysis contained
      in Hl-2261346, Fuel Transfer Canister Drop Analysis (Reference 2), a complete loss of
      shielding was deemed not credible and subsequently removed from the radiological
      consequences analyses prior to review and approval.

  2. Yes. A primary coolant system (PCS) sample will be obtained after fuel assembly DO41
     is placed in the FTC and before the FTC lid is installed. The sample will be analyzed for
     radionuclide concentrations and the results compared with PCS radionuclide
     concentrations established prior to fuel movement.

      The comparison will be used to identify any significant increase in radionuclide
      concentrations that could indicate fuel rod cladding damage or loss of fuel assembly
      fission product barrier integrity resulting from the removal and transfer process. This
      provides a means of assessing fuel integrity before the FTC is closed.

  3. FHS0-19A, Recovery of Fuel Assembly DO41, has a prerequisite, step 3.1.c, that
     requires all fuel assemblies in the reactor vessel West of fuel assembly DO41 to be
     removed from the reactor vessel. DO41 will then be lifted from the reactor vessel to the
     reactor cavity. Once secured within the FTC, DO41 will be lifted from the reactor cavity
     and transported directly to the Equipment Hatch trolley as directed by FHS0-19A. There
     are no safe shutdown SSCs in or in the vicinity of this travel path. While in Containment,
     DO41 will not travel over any fuel assemblies. With DO41 moved on the trolley to the
     Spent Fuel Pool (SFP) side of the Equipment Hatch, DO41 will then be lifted and travel
     North on the West side of the SFP in SFP Heavy Load Path #1 to the North end of the
     SFP. This path will take the canister over the North Tilt Pit where spent fuel is currently
     stored. After reaching the North end, OD41 will then be moved to the Northeast corner of
     the SFP and be placed in the SFP cask laydown area utilizing a portion of SFP Heavy
     Load Path #4. Use of SFP Heavy Load Path #1 is the normal load path used to move all
     material, regardless of weight, in and out of Containment. SFP Heavy Load Path #4 is
     the load path used for moving casks between the cask washdown pit and the SFP.

  4. Assembly DO41 integrity has been qualitatively assessed by underwater camera visual
     examination in preparation for the planned lift from the reactor vessel. In addition ,
     chemistry sampling has been completed to confirm no fuel rod cladding
     damage. Furthermore, the fuel movement device was fabricated accounting for
     information from the qualitative assessment, including the bow of the assembly and the
     deflection of the upper tie plate, and the device is designed to provide positive control of
